claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by understanding the age of the child or children you're claiming for. 

**What is the age of the child (or children) you're asking about?**

Please tell me:
- How many children do you have?
- What is each child's age?

This will help me determine which eligibility pathway to follow. Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualifies automatically
- **16 to 19**: Must meet certain education or training requirements
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, let me proceed with the next step of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 8 years old, we're on the right track. Now I need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

For most 8-year-olds, the answer would be "yes" (not working full-time), but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're just 8, so they're in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school with no paid work, let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check another eligibility criterion:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

In other words - is Alex receiving any of these benefits directly? For an 8-year-old in primary school, the answer would typically be "yes" (meaning they are not receiving these benefits), but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name - they're just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if Alex is in an apprenticeship:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship program?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old and in primary school, I would expect the answer to be "no" - but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - Alex is only 8 and in primary school. They're nowhere near old enough for an apprenticeship!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Let me move forward with the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, which is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

There are several paths that could qualify you:
- You normally live in the UK, OR
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
- You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme and meet certain conditions (working, studying, jobseeking, etc.), OR
- You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Could you let me know your residency situation? The simplest answer for most people would be whether you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm here in England.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward. Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirements. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. This is an important requirement.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You would be considered responsible if ANY of the following apply:
- You live with Alex, OR
- You contribute to Alex's upkeep (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.) at least at the level of the Child Benefit amount, OR
- You're paying maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

For most parents, the answer would be "yes" - but could you confirm your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex lives with you, you're clearly responsible for them. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check something important about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any possibility that another person (such as a former partner, other parent, or grandparent) might be claiming or could claim for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. The possible situations are:
- You're the only person claiming for Alex (straightforward case)
- Someone else is also claiming, but you've agreed who should be the claimant
- There's a dispute about who should claim (which would need HMRC to decide)

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're the only potential claimant for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Where does Alex normally live?**

- Does Alex live at home with you (normal living arrangement)?
- Is Alex currently in hospital?
- Is Alex in care (such as a children's home or other care institution)?
- Is Alex fostered?

Given that you mentioned Alex lives at home with you and is in primary school, I'd expect the answer to be normal living - but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home with me - just a normal living situation. They're not in hospital, care, or fostered or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - Alex is in a normal living situation at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the final step. Just one more question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words - is the council providing financial support for Alex's housing or upkeep? For most families where the child lives at home with their parent(s), the answer would be "yes" (meaning the council is NOT paying) - but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex - we're just a normal family and I support Alex myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I needed to know. You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me provide you with the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful news! Now let me record your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!

**Summary of your eligibility:**

You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for your 8-year-old child, Alex. Here's why:

✓ Alex is under 16 years old  
✓ Alex is not working full-time  
✓ Alex is not receiving any benefits in their own right  
✓ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✓ You live in the UK (England)  
✓ You are responsible for Alex (living with you)  
✓ You are the only claimant for Alex  
✓ Alex is in a normal home environment  
✓ The local council is not paying towards Alex's support  

---

**Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of:**
   - Your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
3. **Be aware:** If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge
4. **Payment frequency:** Payments are made every 4 weeks

**For more information:**
- Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- Contact HMRC Child Benefit team if you have any questions

Congratulations! You should proceed with your application. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

All eligibility criteria are met.
